name: Robin Goodfellow
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Robin Goodfellow is a figure of British folklore. In the play A Midsummer Night's Dream, Shakespeare merged the mischievous fairy Puck with Robin Goodfellow. His father ranked as a ruler among the fairies, a king whose title is often given as Oberon, while his mother was a woman of the mortal world. As a child his mischief grew so great that his mother said she would whip him. He fled and took work with a tailor. He still caused trouble until he faced the same threat once more. He ran off a second time to hunt for his father. From his father he learned how to change his shape. Robin then settled into the life of a diligent and kind brownie.
